# Temple Scroll Column 48 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 48 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 48:1 — "go out to war" vs. "march out to war" vs. "go out to fight" — yatsa la-milchamah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "go out to war" | Literal yatsa |
| LOGOS | "march out to war" | Military register |
| PNEUMA | "go out to fight" | Simplified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "go out to war" per EMET. Literal and well-established biblical idiom.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 48:2 — "brought you up" vs. "brought you up" vs. "brought you out" — he'elah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "brought you up from the land of Egypt" | Literal he'elah — ascent |
| LOGOS | "brought you up from the land of Egypt" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "brought you out of Egypt" | Dynamic — focuses on departure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "brought you up" per EMET and LOGOS. The ascent theology is significant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 48:6 — "goes with you" vs. "marches with you" vs. "is marching with you" — halakh rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the one who goes with you" | Literal halakh |
| LOGOS | "the one who marches with you" | Military context |
| PNEUMA | "is marching with you" | Dynamic present tense |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "goes with you" per EMET. Halakh simply means "to go/walk" — the military connotation is supplied by context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 48:7 — "die in battle" vs. "perish in battle" vs. "die in battle" — muth rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lest he die in battle" | Literal muth |
| LOGOS | "lest he perish in battle" | Formal elevated |
| PNEUMA | "so he does not die in battle" | Modern restructured |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "die in battle" per EMET. Simple and direct.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 48:14 — "is a tree of the field a man" vs. "is the tree of the field a human being" vs. "are trees human beings" — rhetorical question

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "is a tree of the field a man, that it should come under your siege?" | Traditional formulation |
| LOGOS | "is the tree of the field a human being, that it should endure your siege?" | Gender-neutral, formal |
| PNEUMA | "are trees human beings, that you should besiege them too?" | Simplified plural |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's traditional formulation. The singular "tree"/"man" pairing is faithful to the Hebrew and more rhetorically powerful.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 48:16 — "set apart a place" vs. "designate an area" vs. "mark off an area as a latrine area" — camp sanitation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall set apart a place outside the camp" | Literal with deliberate ambiguity |
| LOGOS | "you shall designate an area outside the camp" | Formal administrative |
| PNEUMA | "mark off an area outside the camp as a latrine area" | Explicit interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "set apart a place" per EMET. Preserves the text's own restraint — the function is clear from context without explicit specification.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
